reader.summary: Germany's dominant story this week was the eruption of Gen Z-led cost-of-living protests across more than thirty cities, which escalated from large marches into riots, shop looting, and police clashes, particularly in Frankfurt. The demonstrations were part of a broader European youth mobilisation that also swept France and Italy. On the energy front, Germany missed its winter gas-storage target as a cold snap hit, with storage at record lows, prompting a spat with Italy over rising European gas prices. Chancellor Friedrich Merz completed a multi-country Asia tour spanning South Korea, Japan, and China, where he pushed for wider EU-Asia market access, deepened security ties with Seoul over North Korea, and invited Japan to back a trade alliance. The Eagle's Nest, Hitler's former mountain retreat in the Bavarian Alps, was devastated by a fire and a suspect was detained. Economic signals were mixed: third-quarter growth of 0.2 percent beat expectations, inflation slowed on a fuel-tax cut, and business sentiment rose for a sixth consecutive month, yet consumer confidence slipped. The Audi CEO's appearance at a Trump rally drew union fury, and the debate over who will succeed President Steinmeier intensified, with Merkel calling for the country's first female head of state.

key_events.event: Gen Z protests in over 30 German cities turned violent, with rioters looting shops in Frankfurt and police clashing with demonstrators.
Germany missed its winter gas-storage target as a cold snap set in, with storage levels at a record low, triggering a pricing dispute with Italy.
Chancellor Merz completed an Asia tour visiting South Korea, Japan, and China, proposing wider EU-Asia market access and deepening security cooperation.
A fire devastated the Eagle's Nest retreat built for Hitler in the Bavarian Alps; a suspect was detained.
German economy logged 0.2 percent Q3 growth, faster than expected, while inflation slowed on a fuel-tax cut and business sentiment rose for a sixth month.
Audi's CEO faced union fury and public backlash after appearing at a Trump rally, complicating the company's four-billion-euro deal with the US administration.
The debate over President Steinmeier's successor intensified, with Merkel calling for Germany's first female head of state and several women entering the discussion.
German police arrested two suspects accused of planning sabotage attacks on behalf of Russia, according to Der Spiegel.
Alexander Zverev clinched the world number-one tennis ranking, capping a strong season for German tennis.
An eight-year-old girl was seriously injured in a wolf attack at a German zoo or wildlife park.

display.eli5:
Imagine a bunch of teenagers and young adults are really angry because everything costs too much to buy. They marched in over thirty German cities and some of the marches turned into big fights with police and shops got broken into. Next week, the government will have to figure out what to do about it, and the politicians will argue about whose fault it is and what to fix. This is the Gen Z cost-of-living protest story.

At the same time, Germany didn't fill up its gas tanks before winter, and it's getting cold. That means gas prices are going up and Germany is arguing with Italy about who's to blame. The government might have to start rationing gas for homes. This is the winter gas-storage crisis.

One surprise that could happen is that the boss of Audi got really angry at for going to a rally with the US president, and that could blow up into a bigger fight about how Germany's car companies should deal with America.
